# Vendored `webrtc-ice` 0.17.1

- Upstream: https://github.com/webrtc-rs/webrtc, crate `webrtc-ice` 0.17.1 (as published on crates.io).
- Why vendored: each ICE agent runs one connectivity-check loop (every 200 ms) that awaits every STUN write with no bound. When one local UDP socket stops reporting writable, that write never finishes and the loop stops for good: no more checks, and the controlling agent never nominates. The peer stays in `checking`, or its remote reaches "ICE connected" while DTLS never starts, and nothing times out. Seen on macOS, where host-candidate sockets on the machine's own IPv6 addresses wedged in about 1 of 200-800 concurrent loopback pairs.
- Change: `AgentInternal::send_stun` bounds each STUN write on a UDP candidate by `STUN_SEND_TIMEOUT` (100 ms, `src/agent/agent_config.rs`). A write that does not finish in time is dropped like a lost datagram; STUN retransmits. TCP candidates are not bounded (cancelling a framed write would corrupt the stream). - Change (data writes): `AgentConn::send` bounds each data write (DTLS, SRTP, SCTP) on a UDP pair by `DATA_SEND_TIMEOUT` (100 ms). A write that does not finish in time is dropped like a lost datagram (DTLS and SCTP retransmit), counted in `send_timeouts`, and not counted in `bytes_sent`. Without it, a DTLS ClientHello on a wedged socket hung forever.
- Change (nomination failover): the controlling agent used to re-nominate the same pair every 200 ms for good when that pair never got a success response. `ControllingSelector::contact_candidates` now marks the nominated pair `Failed` after `NOMINATION_FAILOVER_TIMEOUT` (2 s) without an answer and nominates the next valid pair (or pings all candidates when there is none). The controlled agent follows a new nomination: `ControlledSelector` switches its selected pair when a USE-CANDIDATE arrives for a different pair, instead of keeping its first selection forever.
- Change (STUN Binding retransmit): `stun_request` (`src/util/mod.rs`, used by srflx gathering through `get_xormapped_addr` with a 5 s bound) sent one Binding request and waited the whole bound on one read, so one lost UDP datagram cost 5 s of gathering and the srflx candidate, and the first datagram on the socket was taken as the answer whatever its transaction id. It now retransmits with the same transaction id at 0, 0.5, 1.5 and 3.5 s (RTO 500 ms, doubling, RFC 5389 section 7.2.1) and stops at the caller's deadline (the 5 s bound does not grow). Only a Binding success or error response with the request's transaction id is accepted; anything else is ignored and the wait continues. `deadline == 0` keeps one send and an unbounded wait. Upstream `webrtc-ice` has the same single-send function.
- Everything else is byte-identical to the published crate.
- Guard: `src/agent/agent_stun_send_test.rs` (a conn whose writes never complete; both tests fail without the bound), `src/util/stun_retransmit_test.rs` (a loopback STUN responder: a lost first request, gathering an srflx candidate after a lost request, no answer at all (4 sends, 5 s bound), a late answer to the first transmission, a stray datagram first; all but the late-answer case fail without the change) and `src/agent/agent_failover_test.rs` (a nominated pair whose socket wedges fails over and the controlled side follows; a data write on a wedged pair returns within the bound; the controlled agent switches to a new nomination; all three fail without the change). All three run in CI by `scripts/ci/run-pr-integration.sh` ("cargo vendored webrtc-ice").
- Upstream PR: https://github.com/webrtc-rs/webrtc/pull/937 (targets the upstream `v0.17.x` branch; master's sans-IO `rtc-ice` is a rewrite). `webrtc-ice` 0.17.2 on crates.io was published before it and has the same unbounded write.
- Drop the vendored copy and the `[patch.crates-io]` entry once a `webrtc-ice` 0.17.x release containing #937 is published (0.17.3 or later) and the `webrtc` crate we use resolves to it.
